footnotes.text: 3. Students in the Global Studies Program are required to complete foreign language(s) beyond the 122-level required by the College of Arts and Sciences. Students may meet this requirement in two ways: • One language completed through 6 hours at the 300 level, or • Two languages distributed as follows: o Carolina Core GFL language continued through 6 hours at the 200-level, and a o Second language completed through 122 level, which may require from 6-9 hours, depending on whether the language begins with 109 or 121. Note: The number of hours that students must take to fulfill this requirement will depend upon their proficiency in the language, e.g. students who test into 300-level of a language would not need to take the 200-level prerequisites and would only need 6 hours to meet this requirement. Additionally, should students choose to add a foreign language minor or foreign language as a second major and successfully complete course requirements, then this will satisfy the foreign language requirement for the Global Studies major. This requirement may be satisfied through foreign language placement tests.

footnotes.text: 4. The Carolina Core provides the common core of knowledge, skill and academic experience for all Carolina undergraduate students.

evidence.quote: 4. The Carolina Core provides the common core of knowledge, skill and academic experience for all Carolina undergraduate students.

footnotes.text: 5. The College of Arts and Sciences requires one U.S. History and one non-U.S. History course, both of which must be chosen from the approved Carolina Core GHS courses. Whichever is not fulfilled through the Carolina Core GHS requirement must be fulfilled through this college requirement.

footnotes.text: 6. Global Studies Major courses (18 hours): Selection of major courses must include at least one Carolina Core Integrative course: AFAM 366, ANTH 355, ANTH 366, ANTH 371, ANTH 381, ENGL 382, ENGL 434, ENGL 437, ENGL 438D, HIST 305, LASP 301, POLI 315, POLI 316, RUSS 319, RUSS 320 or WGST 381. Of the 24 hours in the major, at least 18 hours must be completed at the 300 level or above. Any courses used to fulfill major requirements may not also fulfill other degree requirements (minor, cognate, Carolina Core) or count toward an additional major. For course options, please see the Bulletin. The Global Studies major consists of three separate components. a. Professional Pathway (9 hours) – Students must complete one Professional Pathway from the following lists. The 9 hours must come from courses listed within a single pathway. Special topics courses with appropriate content may be applied to the Professional Pathways with approval of the advisor. i. Global Development & Sustainability ii. Global Health iii. Global Peace, Conflict, and Human Rights iv. Global Culture b. World Region (9 hours) – Three courses (9 hours) selected from one of the following area studies groups. For course options, please see the Bulletin. Special Topics courses with appropriate content may be applied to the world region requirement with approval of the advisor. i. Africa ii. Asia iii. Europe iv. Latin America and the Caribbean v. Middle East vi. Russia and Eurasia c. Global Thinking (6 hours) – Students must choose at least one of the GLST designated courses or a course cross-listed with a GLST courses (such as FAMS 308). For the remaining three hours, students may choose form the same list or choose three credit hours from the list of comparative courses. For course options, please see the Bulletin. Note: Students are strongly encouraged to spend a period of time overseas, preferably in a country where they can develop their language skills. Participating in a study abroad program or an overseas work experience are two ways to gain an international experience. A period of a semester or full year is most beneficial. Approved study abroad courses may apply to some Global Studies major requirements, with permission of the advisor and the college.
